newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China displays Long March rocket in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: China displays Long March rocket in Hong Kong.

text.p: China put a US$100 million Long March rocket on display in Hong Kong on Saturday.
The rocket, a four-booster giant structure 30 tonnes in weight and 50 metres in length, is the first cluster-type model made by China.
It was first exhibited in Hong Kong in 1991 without the second-stage booster and with a total length of 32 metres.
China's space industry, once much admired for its bargain prices and its strong track record of launch successes, has been plagued by problems in recent years.
Since the beginning of last year, at least two Long March rockets have blown up while another has failed to launch its satellite to the proper orbit.
The string of setbacks for the Chinese space industry has sent insurance premiums for commercial launches soaring, eroding China's price advantage over Western and Japanese competitors.
Several launch contracts with foreign companies were cancelled following the setbacks, partly becasue of concerns over delays due to China's launch backlog.

China says it stil has a high success rate, with only a handful of the 43 launches carried out by its Long March rocket series going wrong. In October, officials said they had tightened safety measures to prevent further disasters.
